# The other invoice the wire covers, settled by its own split.
#
# `INV-USD-002` for 180.00, paid by the −180.00 split of the shared deposit —
# the ordinary Q-016 spelling, one invoice naming the one split that is its
# portion.
#
# It exists to put that split in *this* record's lot, which is what makes it
# not a residue: a split settling another invoice is that invoice's portion
# and was never left over. The writer knows it and skips it; the reader has to
# agree, or a ledger the writer produced is refused by its own importer.
#
# What this fixture produces: `INV-USD-002` settled, its −180.00 split in its
# lot, and the −60.00, −40.00 and −50.00 splits still loose.
#
# Verified by
# tests/integration/test_linking_a_split_not_on_the_receivable.py.
invoice "INV-USD-002"
  customer_id: "C-US"
  currency: USD
  date_opened: 2026-01-07
  entry:
    date: 2026-01-07
    description: "More consulting"
    action: "Hours"
    account: "Income:Sales USD"
    quantity: 1
    price: 180
    taxable: false
    tax_included: false
  posted:
    date: 2026-01-07
    due: 2026-02-07
    ar_account: "Assets:Accounts Receivable USD"
    memo: "Invoice INV-USD-002"
    accumulate: true
  payment:
    date: 2026-03-24
    amount: 180
    account: "Assets:Bank:USD"
    memo: "Wire"
    txn_guid: "77aa11bb22cc33dd44ee55ff66007788"
    txn_split_guid: "bbaa11bb22cc33dd44ee55ff66007744"
